districts.name: The Alderman's Quarter
districts.description: Dunmore's administrative center — town hall, civic offices, the roundabout that is the city's visible center of gravity. Officials move with the harried look of people managing a city on edge. Someone here is either working with the Concord or being used without knowing it.

districts.name: Factor's Row
districts.description: Where goods come in and go out — warehouses, brokers, merchants who know the price of everything. The pamphlets flow through here with the rest of the paper trade. The daily economic engine, currently running about thirty percent angrier than usual.

districts.name: Tinker's Row
districts.description: Dense, practical streets of workshops and small trades. The craftspeople here have been angry longer than the pamphlets have existed. That's what makes them useful. The Old Hill's working heart, where the city's actual labor happens without ceremony.

districts.name: Ink Quarter
districts.description: Archives, booksellers, scribes, and the city's intellectual fringe. Whoever organized the propaganda campaign knew this neighborhood well — the paper supply, the distribution networks, the people who ask too many questions and the ones who don't ask enough.

districts.name: The Carouse
districts.description: The city's busy commercial and social heart — taverns, inns, lodging, trades. Where Dunmore's mood is loudest and most legible. Cael Darro chose this neighborhood to operate in for a reason: it's where the city talks.

districts.name: Songbird's Way
districts.description: The social tier above the Carouse — fashionable establishments, haberdashers, tailors, and gathering places for the aspirational class. Music and managed appearances. The residents here have opinions about the pamphlets but express them at dinner parties, not street corners.

districts.name: The Devotion
districts.description: A small but well-tended religious enclave at the city's center. Healing is available to anyone who needs it. The silence here is conspicuous given how loud the rest of Dunmore has become — the priests have noticed the injuries, and they are quietly angry.

districts.name: Rampart Row
districts.description: The Watch's operational base, adjacent to the Alderman's Quarter. The orders that come from here lately have been quietly unusual — specific streets to patrol, specific complaints not to pursue. Someone in the civic structure is managing what the Watch sees.

districts.name: Crestview
districts.description: The oldest money in Dunmore — estates, private clubs, and the studied indifference of people who can afford to be wrong. Currently hosting several unfamiliar guests who are better connected than they have any obvious reason to be.

districts.name: Alley Row
districts.description: The streets that appeared faster than the city could plan them. The poorest residents, the newest arrivals, and the people who end up here when everywhere else has no room. The anger here is real, even if the cause is manufactured.

districts.name: The Manufactory
districts.description: Workshops, foundries, and the city's grinding productive core. The workers here are the quietest political force in Dunmore — so far. The pamphlets have reached here too, passed hand to hand between shifts.

districts.name: The Shrines
districts.description: A cluster of minor shrines and devotional spaces on the city's eastern edge. Frequented by the Lanes' respectable class, who prefer their religion at a slight remove from the noise. The head priest here has been conspicuously quiet about the propaganda.

initial.description: Dunmore's seat of government, anchoring the roundabout at the Alderman's Quarter. Guards are posted. Officials move with the harried look of people managing a city on edge.

explored.description: Concord operatives have been observed using a side entrance reserved for messengers. Someone inside is either working with them or being used without knowing it.

fully_explored.description: The town hall served as a Concord information node — operatives monitored the propaganda campaign's political effect from here.

secrets.text: At least one official has been receiving payments traceable to the printing operation.
Cael Darro used this building's messenger network to position himself in Dunmore before the party arrived.

initial.description: One of the larger private estates in Crestview. Frequent gatherings — wine, debate, the usual performance of influence.

explored.description: Mirelle Voss has been a fixture here for the past month. She is better connected than she has any obvious reason to be.

fully_explored.description: Mirelle used Haverstock's network to map who in Dunmore could be bought, managed, or made to look away. Assessment operation, not socializing.

secrets.text: Mirelle attended as 'Sera Vantalle', a merchant's widow from the southern provinces.
It was Mirelle who identified the party as useful and arranged for Cael Darro to be here when they arrived.

initial.description: A private members' club for the town's upper crust. No sign. The door is answered before you knock.

explored.description: The Club's membership overlaps heavily with Mirelle Voss's social calendar. Several members have made donations to funds with no public record.

initial.description: A well-maintained temple to the goddess of civilization and law. Attended by the Lanes' respectable class. Services are formal. Donations are visible.

explored.description: Head priest Brother Aldric Vane has been conspicuously quiet about the propaganda. He preaches order — order that doesn't require asking where the pamphlets come from.

fully_explored.description: Brother Vane received a quiet donation from a 'civic beautification fund' that appears in no public record. His silence was purchased.

secrets.text: The donation was Concord money. Vane's silence on the propaganda was bought — not cheaply, and not without his understanding what he agreed to.

initial.description: A respected haberdasher: hats, caps, gloves, fine small wares. Old Barrow notices everything and forgets nothing.

explored.description: Barrow has seen unfamiliar faces moving through the quarter — men and women who don't belong to any household he recognizes. He will talk if asked carefully.

initial.description: A scrivener and notary. Contracts, letters of introduction, legal documents. Efficient and discreet.
The best stables in Dunmore. Horses boarded, hired, or bought. The grooms are professional and don't ask about your hours.
A clean, unremarkable inn for travelers of modest means. Full most nights. The common room runs warmer than usual lately.
A modest shrine to the goddess of luck and travel. Travelers pray here before the road; merchants before a deal. Kept by Tessaly, who hears a great deal.

explored.description: Tessaly distinguishes carefully between information and secrets. She is not a gossip — but she remembers what she's told, and sometimes shares it when reason presents itself.

initial.description: Everything you might need and nothing you'd linger over. Good prices, indifferent service, reliable stock.
Currency exchange and informal credit. The ledgers here are not public and the rates are not posted.

explored.description: Several large transactions have passed through here that don't match any legitimate business on this street.

secrets.text: The transactions are Concord funds being distributed to local intermediaries — the printing operation's supply chain runs through here.

initial.description: A dense cluster of food carts at the market's widest intersection. Bread, roasted meats, pies, cheap wine. Pamphlets appear between purchases.

explored.description: The cart owners didn't choose to distribute pamphlets — they appeared one morning, already stacked. None of the vendors will confirm or deny passing them on.

initial.description: The most popular tavern in the Carouse — loud, full, running about thirty percent angrier than usual. The barkeep keeps his opinions to himself.

explored.description: Cael Darro is a regular here — losing at cards gracefully, buying rounds, listening. He fits in too well. He has been here before the party arrived.

fully_explored.description: The Crossed Keys was Cael Darro's primary observation post. The corner table has sightlines to both doors. The barkeep has been paid to be incurious.

secrets.text: Cael's regular table has sightlines to both doors. He has been coming here since before the party arrived in Dunmore.

initial.description: A working tailor — repairs, alterations, commissions. Backed up two weeks on orders.
A jeweler serving the upper market. Rings, pendants, small valuables — and a discreet appraisal service for items whose provenance you'd rather not discuss.
Dunmore's dedicated bookseller. Proprietor Mira remembers every customer and every purchase.

explored.description: Someone has been buying up every regional map Mira can source. She was asked to be discreet about it — will confirm only that the buyer was not a local.

secrets.text: The regional maps were purchased by a Concord operative mapping movement corridors in the area.

initial.description: Shaves, haircuts, teeth pulled, minor wounds dressed. Renwick sees a lot of faces and remembers most of them. Has been busier than usual.
Tools, hardware, basic weapons, repair work. Tam Ashford has been quietly declining orders for anything longer than a short sword.

explored.description: Tam has heard things at the forge — conversations men have when they assume fire drowns out voices. He's turning down weapon orders because he doesn't want to know what they're for.

initial.description: Market stalls specializing in dried spices, culinary herbs, and imported flavourings. Fragrant, cheerful, and blissfully apolitical.
A patrol staging post for the Watch. Two guards on rotation, usually looking bored or anxious depending on the hour.

explored.description: The watch has been given specific orders about which streets to patrol — and specific orders about which complaints not to pursue.

secrets.text: The Watch's standing orders on certain streets came down from the Town Hall two months ago. No explanation was given.

initial.description: The city's official posting board. Currently buried under anti-Elkenquay pamphlets three layers deep.

explored.description: An old gatehouse at the boundary of the Alderman's Quarter. After the monstrosity attack, this is where the Concord extracted the party.

fully_explored.description: The extraction point was pre-selected. Cael Darro knew in advance where the attack would drive the crowd. The rescue was choreographed, not reactive.

secrets.text: Chaelynn was already here before the party arrived. She had been positioned before the monstrosity was released. She knew it was coming.

initial.description: A small apothecary on an unnamed side-street — just a grey vial hung above the door. Stocks potions, wands, and components. Proprietor Orvyn asks no questions.

explored.description: Orvyn maintains a secondary stock not on display — substances that are legal in some jurisdictions.

fully_explored.description: Orvyn has had at least one Concord contact as a regular customer. He appears to still be alive — which suggests the Concord considers him useful.

secrets.text: Orvyn supplied alchemical compounds used to treat the propaganda paper, making it water-resistant. He knew what it was for.

initial.description: A small healing chapel. Sister Hadara runs it on donations and determination. Healing available to anyone who needs it.

explored.description: Sister Hadara has been treating more injuries than usual — men who won't say what happened. She is quietly angry about it.

initial.description: A cluttered pawnshop at the market's edge. Aldous buys without asking and sells without explaining. Everything here came from somewhere unpleasant.
An old building on a back street of Tinker's Row. Windows covered. Faint smell of ink. The door latch shows fresh wear.

explored.description: The source of the anti-Elkenquay propaganda. Organized, funded, and deliberately targeted. This is not amateur agitation.

fully_explored.description: A Concord instrument. The pamphlet campaign is part of a manufactured crisis. A resonance artifact was stored here.

secrets.text: The funding runs through three intermediaries, each using the same courier. Paper supply routed through a warehouse in the lower market.
The Concord runs this operation as part of a larger strategy requiring a destabilized region.

explored.description: A respectable lodging house near the Carouse. Chaelynn has been staying here — a familiar face the party trusts. Her presence in Dunmore is not a coincidence.

fully_explored.description: Chaelynn was placed here deliberately. She has been observing the party throughout the Prologue and reporting to Cael Darro.

secrets.text: A letter in Chaelynn's room, in cipher, is addressed to 'C.D.' How much of her friendship was a Concord instrument is deliberately left unanswered.

initial.description: A busy intersection in Tinker's Row where pamphlets change hands openly. Men argue about Elkenquay here before breakfast. The anger is real, even if the cause is manufactured.

explored.description: A specific figure distributes pamphlets here each morning — always gone before the watch change, always from a new stack.

secrets.text: The distributor picks up fresh stock from a dead drop two streets away, tracing back to a warehouse in the lower market.

initial.description: The cheapest rooms in Dunmore. Thin walls, no questions, a lock that mostly works. Full of people with somewhere to be and no one to tell.
Shoes, belts, straps, leather repair. Slow, thorough, cheap. Works by the window and sees everyone on the lane.
